source: make a tower defence game the has cool guns and make teleporters to host games and make people start with scout and wall and make scout have a gun and make it so the path in the hosted game if you place a wall on the path it changes ways and make futuristic stuff like the moonbuster from rapid infection | 2 | the rapid expansion and other stuff like the bulwark mech and normal mech from elite mech pilot and mech pilot and other stuff from that game

image_prompt.text: Open buildable ground either side of the path where players drop walls and gun turrets
The goal structure at the end of the path that the enemies are trying to reach
Pinch points in the route where waves bunch up
sleek futuristic hardware dressing the battlefield - a heavy long-range cannon emplacement and standing mech units, a bulwark type and a standard type, used as props around the field
teleporter pads for hosting and joining games

layout_placement.text: The mouth of the path where each enemy wave enters
The end-of-path goal marker representing the defenders' health pool
teleporter markers that send a player into a hosted game

notes: The shape is wrong and was kept anyway. lane-actor-track is defined as a single continuous, unchanging lane, and this prompt's central mechanic is that placing a wall on the path reroutes it. A maze-style recomputed path has no shape in this genre.
P6 generates one valid route once; nothing validates that every wall placement still leaves a legal route.
The named references (Moonbuster, Bulwark mech, mechs from another game) are outside assets and were reduced to generic futuristic props.

open_questions.ask: When a wall reroutes the path, should the enemies find any route across open ground, or only follow a few pre-authored alternate lanes?
The named mechs are from other games - should these be generic futuristic stand-ins?

theme: Futuristic sci-fi military - mechs and high-tech weaponry

coverage_missing.ask: Is the rerouting free-form pathfinding across open ground, or a switch between a few fixed lanes?
What are the enemies attacking, and what ends a round?
How big is the battlefield - one compact arena, or a large field with several routes?
Should the mechs and the heavy cannon be generic futuristic props, since the named ones belong to other games?

answers.ask: When a wall reroutes the path, should the enemies find any route across open ground, or only follow a few pre-authored alternate lanes?
answers.answer: Enemies should dynamically find a route across the open ground when walls block their current path, so wall placement genuinely changes their route.

answers.ask: The named mechs are from other games - should these be generic futuristic stand-ins?
answers.answer: Use generic futuristic stand-ins inspired by the broad role and feel of those units, not direct copies of the named mechs or items.
